Waking up several times during the night to urinate may seem like a normal part of aging, but frequent nighttime urination, also known as nocturia, can have several underlying causes.

In this 21-minute video, Healing and Health explains how aging, changes in ADH (vasopressin), kidney function, blood sugar, circulation, and fluid retention can contribute to nighttime bathroom trips. You’ll also discover how fluid pooling in your legs during the day may return to your bloodstream when you lie down, increasing urine production at night.

What really happens to your body after 80? In this video, Healing and Health explores five important changes associated with aging: muscle loss, changes in sleep and brain health, weaker bones, balance problems, and chronic inflammation.

Discover how protein-rich nutrition, gentle exercise, balance training, quality sleep, and healthy eating may support strength and independence in later life. Whether you're over 80 or caring for an older loved one, these research-based insights can help you better understand healthy aging.

📚 Research Sources:

ESPEN and PROT-AGE Study Group — Clinical Nutrition (2014).

Hablitz et al. — Nature Communications (2024).
